companions.value: PR changes: reads the PR as data, runs none of its code.
A description is text, not code: a failure is the author's to fix in the PR's description, not a change autofix can make.

fog-and-frontier.why: fog-and-frontier's header and `scenarios` description name its own scenarios folder (scripts/gif-scenarios/) and its production build, which the canonical says generically.

sift.why: sift's CI is the recording, so its caller is the dispatch half only (workflow_dispatch, no pull_request), with `actions: write` on the job and `scenarios` defaulting to empty.

companions.value: Records the PR's GIF scenarios; a failed recording is a scenario or the app to look at, not code autofix can fix.

sift.why: sift's CI is the recording, so its attach caller waits for the workflow "CI" (not "PR GIFs"), runs only for a pull_request run, and has `actions: write` on the job.

unsynced.why: A reusable workflow the apps call at @main; their callers are synced above (gif/callers/pr-gif.yml).
A reusable workflow the apps call at @main; their callers are synced above (gif/callers/pr-gif-attach.yml).
A reusable workflow the apps call at @main from a visual-review.yml of their own, which names the workflows each app's screenshots come from, so the callers differ by design.
A reusable workflow the apps call at @main from a weekly-audit.yml of their own; no canonical caller exists yet.
A reusable workflow the apps call at @main from a mutation-sweep.yml of their own, on the app's own schedule; no canonical caller exists yet.
A reusable workflow the apps call at @main as a job of their own workflows (ci.yml and others), so no file of an app is a copy of it.
